chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the one in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) immerses himself in the water with one immersion, that suffices him for his ritual bath (ghusl).'

key_terms.أَجْزَأَهُ: It sufficed him / It was accepted as sufficient.
key_terms.ارْتِمَاسَةً: Immersion or plunging the body into water.
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The person in a state of major ritual impurity, typically after sexual intercourse or ejaculation.
key_terms.غُسْلِهِ: The ritual bath (ghusl) required to remove major impurity.

ai.seo_question: How many times must one immerse in water to perform a valid ghusl for major impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the minimal requirement for ghusl al-janabah, establishing that a single complete immersion (irtimas) suffices, a view often contrasted with the Shia emphasis on ensuring water reaches all parts of the body through deliberate movement. It reflects the juristic principle that the obligation is fulfilled by the act of immersion itself, provided the water covers the entire body, distinguishing it from wudu where specific limbs are washed sequentially. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the mechanics of purification, prioritizing the certainty of water contact over rigid procedural repetitions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When the one with sexual impurity immerses himself into the water with one immersion that would suffice him from his washing’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘If one, for Ghusl (bath) because of sexual relation, immerses oneself in water once, it is sufficient.’”
